# Funding as carry and short squeeze dynamics — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Funding as carry and short squeeze dynamics. Run status: COMPLETED.

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Funding-rate arbitrage (long spot, short perp), the capital that takes the other side of leveraged long demand, is not risk-free. He et al.: it 'is not risk-free even disregarding margin requirements and trading costs, simply because there is no predetermined expiration date when the trade would be unwound at a profit', and temporary worsening of apparent arbitrage opportunities 'can lead to liquidations and losses'. BIS: engaging in cash-and-carry is risky because of spikes in margins and liquidations amid drawdowns. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2212.06888v7 · keywords: Funding as carry and short squeeze dynamics · also: https://www.bis.org/publ/work1087.pdf

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Auto-deleveraging (ADL) can close winning shorts. Hyperliquid: if an account's value or isolated position value goes negative, opposite-side users are ranked by unrealized PnL and leverage using (mark_price / entry_price) x (notional_position / account_value), and are closed at the previous mark price. FTI: on 2025-10-10 'some of the best-hedged shorts found their positions reduced or entirely closed', which can turn a hedged portfolio into a naked one. BitMEX: ADL across multiple exchanges disrupted delta-neutral strategies, forced professional market makers to cut liquidity, and left order books at their thinnest since 2022. (high confidence) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/auto-deleveraging · keywords: Funding as carry and short squeeze dynamics · also: https://fticonsulting.com/insights/articles/crypto-crash-october-2025-leverage-met-liquidity, https://www.aap.com.au/aapreleases/globenewswire1001158221/
